key_insight: Dynin-Robotics unifies language, vision, goals, and robot actions in one diffusion-based model, so the same backbone can predict desired outcomes and generate actions. This lets a robot choose actions that are jointly guided by a target scene and expected scene dynamics.
problem_solved: Robotic policies often struggle to connect natural-language instructions with both what the scene should look like and how actions will change it. This paper addresses the need for a single model that can condition on language and visual context while generating useful robot trajectories.
method: Uses Dynin-Omni, an omnimodal masked-diffusion backbone, to represent language, visual observations, goals, and actions as discrete tokens.
Forms a shared trajectory model that can flexibly vary conditioning and prediction spans, enabling both goal prediction and action generation/selection.
Integrates visual goal and dynamics prediction directly into the action generation process for language-conditioned robot control.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a unified framework for multimodal robot policy learning instead of separate modules for perception, goal planning, and control. It may improve generalization and make robot behavior more coherent by aligning predicted goals with action-dependent scene changes.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing language, images, goals, and actions all feeding into one diffusion model.

Two-path illustration comparing goal prediction vs. action generation from the same backbone.

paper_title: Dynin-Robotics: Omnimodal Unified Diffusion Vision-Language-Action Model
paper_authors: Hoeun Lee, Jaeik Kim, Jusang Oh, Jinhyeok Kim, Geon Choi
